title: Quantized eval playlog - daybook
content:
Quick notes / daybook for quantized eval runs, heuristics to try, and TODOs. This is very much a scratchpad — messy, terse, and time-ordered.

2026-03-09 09:15 — morning coffee, set up baseline
- baseline model: llama-2-13b-chat (fp16) served on dev-gpu-a
- baseline prompts: small instruction set (see prompt set v1 below)
- baseline metrics captured: p95 latency 82ms / token, throughput ~320 tok/sec on batch=1, mem 21.6GB
- goal: match baseline quality within <2% perplexity increase while reducing per-token cost by ~2-3x via quantization + KV cache reuse

Things I want to capture in this doc:
- quick hyperparams to try for PTQ and QAT-ish workflows
- prompt variants and deterministic eval set (20 short dialogs + 40 long context ones)
- observations about KV cache retention and weird memory jitter seen on dev-gpu-b
- checklist for shipping a candidate quantized variant to staging

Prompt set v1 (short):
- InstrShort-1: "Summarize the article in one sentence."
- InstrShort-2: "List 3 pros and 2 cons of X."
- InstrShort-3: "Translate to casual tone: <input>"

Prompt set v1 (long context):
- LongCtx-1: 2k prefix with doc excerpt, question: "What are the three most risk-prone areas?"
- LongCtx-2: 4k prefix (split into two messages) - test KV cache hit behaviour across segments

Experiment log (notes):
- 2026-03-09 11:03 — run: post-training static quant (GPTQ-like), 4-bit NF4, layerwise grouping=128
  * model: llama-2-13b-ptq-4bit-nf4
  * perf: p95 token latency 58ms (improvement), throughput +1.4x, mem down to 11.2GB
  * quality spot-check (InstrShort set): BLEU-like heuristics show ~1.8% drop, human quick read is fine for short answers
  * failure modes: hallucination rate up on LongCtx-2 (answers drop cohesion after 2.5k tokens)
  * hypothesis: aggressive 4-bit quant on attention matmuls introduces small numeric drift that compounds for long context; KV cache compression might hurt recurrence

- 2026-03-09 14:10 — run: clipped KV cache + adaptive padding
  * change: truncate older KV entries older than 800 tokens, pad sequence to 64-step blocks to stabilize kernel loads
  * result: small latency variance reduction (p95 now 53ms), but accuracy on LongCtx declines further
  * note: need an experiment measuring tradeoff: KV retention length vs accuracy vs latency

- 2026-03-10 09:45 — run: QLoRA-style adapter fine-tune on 512M tokens (toy), then PTQ 4-bit NF4
  * model: llama-2-13b-qlora-ptq-4bit
  * perf: slightly better coherence on LongCtx (subjective), p95 60ms, mem 12GB
  * note: QLoRA adapters seem to regrow some robustness for long-range dependencies; cost to reproduce is nontrivial

- 2026-03-10 16:20 — found a weird SRE-ish jitter on dev-gpu-b when batching burst>8
  * symptom: token throughput drops 2x for a ~4s window then recovers; repeated with same workload
  * hypothesis: kernel eviction/fragmentation in driver, or our allocator failing to pre-warm kernels for 4-bit paths
  * action: file issue, capture nsys trace, ping infra (#infra-kernel)

Quick micro-checks to add to CI (low-effort):
- synthetic test: determinism under quantized weights for fixed seed across 10 runs (short prompts)
- long-run stability: run 50 sample long-context prompts back-to-back and check reply length + token distribution drift
- latency regression: ensure p95 of quantized variant < 1.2x baseline for short prompts

TODO list (priority):
- [ ] add deterministic synthetic tests to small-run CI (ENG-4821)
- [ ] capture nsys trace for kernel jitter and attach to issue (need infra help)
- [ ] run ablation: NF4 vs INT4 symmetric vs per-channel scaling on 3 layers (log results)
- [ ] try hybrid scheme: first N layers fp16, last M layers 4-bit, measure tradeoff (N=6, M=7)
- [ ] prepare a short one-pager for product on safety/quality implications of quantization (for PM review)

Notes on quant config I tried:
- config A: 4bit-nf4, group=128, clamp=0.0, perchannel=True
- config B: 4bit-int, group=64, clamp=0.1, perchannel=False (slightly faster on one kernel path)
- config C: hybrid fp16-first6 + 4bit-last7 (good latency, best coherent answers so far)

Small checklist to promote candidate to staging:
- performance benchmark (latency + throughput) vs baseline (attach CSV)
- regression tests (determinism, long-run stability) green
- safety: sample hallucination heuristics, toxic-token check (score threshold)
- docs: short README for inference config + known failure modes
- rollback plan: fallback route configured in console (use fp16 variant)

Ideas / rough heuristics (brain dump):
- if long-context quality drops >3% relative to baseline, avoid 4-bit-only in staged production for customer-facing chat flows
- hybrid quantization (preserve first X layers) often recovers coherence at small cost; tune X per model size
- KV cache pruning should be workload-aware: threshold by token importance (attention score proxy) rather than naive age

Random commands / snippets used recently:
- run bench: python bench/run_infer.py --model ./models/llama-13b-4bit --batch 1 --prompts prompts/short.json --trace nsys_open
- convert ptq: ./tools/ptq_quantize --model models/13b/fp16 --out models/13b-4bit --group 128 --nf4
- sample eval script header: python scripts/eval_prompts.py --model model-path --prompts prompts/long.json --seed 42 --max-length 1024 --metrics rouge,bleu,sim

Open questions to resolve:
- what is the appropriate p95 latency SLO for hosted-labs vs dedicated? affects how aggressive we can be
- how to standardize the long-context human eval so product signoff is consistent (we need 3 raters?)
- is there a quick quant-aware dropout test to simulate numeric instability?

Last notes (2026-03-12 10:05):
- shared quick results with Ava; she suggested trying mixed-precision matmul kernel (driver flag) that might avoid eviction jitter
- next session: reproduce jitter with nsys + try config C with longer adapter fine-tune (2x steps) and check hallucination metric on LongCtx-2

Finished for now — will archive good runs to models/quant-candidates/ with one-line summary and csv metrics.
